figures.caption: Figure 1: Recordings are processed by a pretrained encoder, yielding representations that are jointly modeled across time and streams over the complete night using a mask-aware state-space network.
Table 1: Pooled out-of-fold AUROC without (A) and with (B) demographic and anthropometric covariates. Best and second-best results per panel are bolded and underlined, respectively.

Figure 2: Downstream performance without covariates. Left: labeled-data efficiency; points and error bars denote mean out-of-fold AUROC and one standard deviation across participant-level draws. Right: macro-AUROC using linear probing and missingness-aware state-space modeling.

Table 2: Characteristics of the BSWR analysis cohort. Demographic and diagnostic distributions are reported at the recording level, corresponding to the unit of prediction. Diagnostic categories are non-mutually exclusive.
Table 3: Canonical PSG signal families supplied to at least one evaluated encoder.

Table 6: Pooled out-of-fold AUROC under common-core input coverage, without (A) and with (B) demographic and anthropometric covariates. Best and second-best available results per panel are bolded and underlined.

Table 8: Downstream data efficiency under each encoder’s full physiological input coverage, without demographic and anthropometric covariates. Reduced-data values are mean ± standard deviation across participant draws. Best and second-best mean AUROCs within each training fraction and outcome are bolded and underlined, respectively.

Table 9: Downstream data efficiency under non-respiratory core, without demographic and anthropometric covariates. Reduced-data values are mean ± standard deviation across participant-level draws. Best and second-best reported mean AUROCs within each training fraction and outcome are bolded and underlined, respectively.
